statement: Kaleigh Trace (born 1986) is a Canadian writer, sex educator, and therapist based in Toronto, Ontario known for her candid discussions of sexuality and disability.
Her 2014 memoir Hot, Wet, and Shaking: How I Learned to Talk About Sex chronicles her experiences as a disabled, queer, feminist sex educator.
The memoir Hot, Wet, and Shaking: How I Learned to Talk About Sex won the 2015 Evelyn Richardson Memorial Non-Fiction Award at the Atlantic Book Awards.
Trace and her family experienced a car accident in 1995.
The car accident left Trace with a severe injury to her spinal cord.
As a result of the accident, Trace spent part of her childhood in a wheelchair.
Trace graduated from Dalhousie University with a Bachelor of Arts in 2009.
Trace subsequently became employed at Venus Envy, a Canadian sex shop and book retailer.
Trace's work at Venus Envy included sex education.
Trace credited her time at Venus Envy with expanding her knowledge on human sexuality.
While working at Venus Envy, Trace began writing a blog, The Fucking Facts.
In her blog, The Fucking Facts, Trace discussed deeply personal topics such as an abortion she had two years prior to starting the blog.
Trace's blog, The Fucking Facts, served as inspiration for her book Hot, Wet, and Shaking.
In 2013, Trace received internet attention for her parody song of Blurred Lines by Robin Thicke entitled Ask First.
The song Ask First was co-written by Trace and other Venus Envy staff members.
The memoir Hot, Wet, and Shaking details Trace's experience as a disabled, queer, feminist sex educator.
The memoir explores Trace's personal story with sexuality through the lens of her spinal cord injury and work at Venus Envy.
Through honest and humorous anecdotes, Trace challenges conventional narratives of sex.
The book Hot, Wet, and Shaking covers topics from struggles with orgasm and comical mishaps to serious issues like abortion and ableism.
Trace remained employed at Venus Envy until moving to Toronto in 2017.
Trace commuted to study at the University of Guelph, where she received her Master of Science in couples and family therapy.
Trace worked at a Toronto therapy clinic before eventually opening a private practice.
In October 2022, Trace was diagnosed with terminal bladder cancer.
In 2022, Trace was contacted by Invisible Publishing regarding the republication of a 10-year anniversary edition of Hot, Wet, and Shaking.
Trace agreed to the republication, calling the book a 'much-needed celebration of sex'.
The republished book included a new introduction, as well as chapters reflecting her cancer diagnosis.
For the launch of the 10-year anniversary edition, Trace hosted a performance event including standup comedy, games, and reading of short stories.
The success of the event led to Trace hosting another performance called Little Deaths Salon in Toronto with Christa Couture in July 2025.
The Little Deaths Salon performance is returning on 17 October 2025 at the Buddies in Bad Times Theatre.
Trace's memoir, Hot, Wet, and Shaking: How I Learned to Talk About Sex, was first published on 17 September 2014 by Invisible Publishing of Halifax, Nova Scotia.
The book Hot, Wet, and Shaking draws from Trace's experiences as a disabled, queer, feminist sex educator at Venus Envy.
The book Hot, Wet, and Shaking explores Trace's personal story with sexuality, shaped by a spinal cord injury from a car accident in 1995, through candid and humorous anecdotes.
The book Hot, Wet, and Shaking addresses topics such as struggles with orgasm, abortion, ableism, and the complexities of sexual identity.
The book Hot, Wet, and Shaking challenges conventional narratives surrounding sex and disability.
The book Hot, Wet, and Shaking was praised for its balance of humour and emotion.
The praise for the book noted Trace's ability to seamlessly transition between recounting comical mishaps and reflecting on serious topics.
In 2014, Hot, Wet, and Shaking was named the gold winner for best book by The Coast, a Halifax newspaper.
In 2017, Hot, Wet, and Shaking was listed among 150 Books of Influence by the Nova Scotia Library Association.
A German translation of the book Hot, Wet, and Shaking was released in 2020.
The German translation was published by Orlanda Verlag of Berlin.
The book Hot, Wet, and Shaking was translated by Penelope Dützmann, a linguistics professor at the University of Cologne.
The German translation of the book was presented at the 2021 Frankfurt Book Fair as part of Canada's Guest of Honor appearance in collaboration with the Canadian Embassy in Germany.
A 10th anniversary edition of the book Hot, Wet, and Shaking was published in 2024, also by Invisible Publishing.
The revised 10th anniversary edition includes a new introduction, as well as new chapters reflecting on Trace's cancer diagnosis two years prior to the republication.
The new chapters offer further insight into Trace's evolving perspective on the topics of sex and mortality.
In 2024, the book Hot, Wet, and Shaking was listed on The Hamilton Review of Books' bestsellers list for July 2024.
Kaleigh Trace published "Hot, Wet, and Shaking: How I Learned To Talk About Sex" in 2014 with Invisible Publishing in Halifax, NS.
The 2014 edition of "Hot, Wet, and Shaking: How I Learned To Talk About Sex" has ISBN 978-1-9267-4347-9.
The 2014 edition of "Hot, Wet, and Shaking: How I Learned To Talk About Sex" has OCLC 1028583483.
Kaleigh Trace published "Hot, Wet & Shaking: Wie ich lernte über Sex zu sprechen" (in German) in 2020 with Orlanda Verlag in Berlin, Germany.
The German edition of "Hot, Wet & Shaking" was translated by Penelope Dützmann.
The German edition of "Hot, Wet & Shaking" has ISBN 978-3-9446-6661-7.
The German edition of "Hot, Wet & Shaking" has OCLC 1348605874.
Kaleigh Trace published "Hot, Wet, and Shaking: How I Learned To Talk About Sex (Tenth Anniversary ed.)" in 2024 with Invisible Publishing in Halifax, NS.
The Tenth Anniversary edition of "Hot, Wet, and Shaking: How I Learned To Talk About Sex" has ISBN 978-1-7784-3046-6.
The Tenth Anniversary edition of "Hot, Wet, and Shaking: How I Learned To Talk About Sex" has OCLC 1464921208.
Kaleigh Trace published the article "WILD ACTS: On Resistance in Sex and Body" in GUTS Canadian Feminist Magazine, No. 3, in Toronto, ON, on 16 December 2014.
Kaleigh Trace published the article "Getting Down With Getting Off" in Shameless Magazine, No. 30, in Toronto, ON, by Shameless Media, in Fall 2015.
Kaleigh Trace published the article "What a radical restructuring of Canada's health care system would look like" in This Magazine, in Toronto, ON, by Red Maple Foundation, on 9 November 2016.
Kaleigh Trace published the article "6 LGBTQ Canadians weigh in on being queer in 2017" in CBC News (Canada 2017) by the Canadian Broadcasting Corporation on 13 July 2017.
